title: The next tier of what is asked for — 11 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
The next tier of what is asked for. 11 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/demand2.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. 8 are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). 3 are proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 2 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 13 pairs; the theorems fall into 7 strands, the largest of 5. Most binding: sumPow (5), tri (3). 1 theorem names no definition of the file and stands on its own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: families.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 2 files: src/proof/demand2.lean, src/proof/families.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 11 sealed receipts fold to 02ef7200-8f0b-82b3-a349-6b0f01112b10. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (6, 0, 7, 0, 4, 8, 5). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: reversal.lean (4 observed, 1.5 expected, lift 2.66), coin.lean (3 observed, 1.29 expected, lift 2.33), energy.lean (4 observed, 2.36 expected, lift 1.7). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 3.33 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 72.0% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.62; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.52. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 95155bc810f5 (2026-09-15), over 719 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. Wilson’s theorem — John Wilson; first proved by Joseph-Louis Lagrange, 1771; the Catalan conjecture on consecutive perfect powers — Eugène Catalan, 1844; proved by Preda Mihăilescu, 2002. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. nicomachus_sum_of_cubes_is_the_square_of_the_triangular_number — (List.range' 1 40).all (fun n => sumPow 3 n == tri n * tri n) ∧ (List.range' 1 40).all (fun n => sumPow 3 n == sumPow 1 n * sumPow 1 n) ∧ (List.range' 2 19).all (fun n => ¬ isSquareBelow 900 (sumPow 4 n)) ∧ isSquareBelow 900 (sumPow 4 1) = true record
  2. picks_theorem_holds_for_every_lattice_triangle_in_the_four_grid — pts.all (fun a => pts.all (fun b => pts.all (fun c => cross a b c ≤ 0 || cross a b c == 2 * interiorCount a b c + boundaryCount a b c - 2))) ∧ ¬ pts.any (fun a => pts.any (fun b => pts.any (fun c => cross a b c > 0 && cross a b c == 2 * interiorCount a b c + boundaryCount a b c))) ∧ (triples.filter (fun t => cross t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2 > 0)).length = 1548 ∧ (triples.filter (fun t => cross t.1 t.2.1 t.2. … record
  3. bezouts_identity_is_attained_and_no_smaller_combination_exists — (List.range' 1 30).all (fun a => (List.range' 1 30).all (fun b => (List.range 31).any (fun x => (List.range 31).any (fun y => a * x == b * y + Families.gcd' a b)))) ∧ (List.range' 1 20).all (fun a => (List.range' 1 20).all (fun b => (List.range 21).all (fun x => (List.range 21).all (fun y => a * x < b * y || (a * x - b * y) % Families.gcd' a b == 0)))) ∧ Families.gcd' 240 46 = 2 ∧ 46 * 47 = 240 * … record
  4. the_latin_squares_of_order_four_number_five_hundred_and_seventy_six — latinSquares 4 = 576 ∧ latinSquares 3 = 12 ∧ latinSquares 2 = 2 ∧ latinSquares 1 = 1 ∧ ¬ (latinSquares 4 = 24 * 24 * 24) record
  5. the_sum_of_fifth_powers_has_the_closed_form_asked_for — (List.range' 1 20).all (fun n => 12 * sumPow 5 n == n * n * (n + 1) * (n + 1) * (2 * n * n + 2 * n - 1)) ∧ (List.range' 2 19).all (fun n => ¬ (sumPow 5 n == tri n * tri n * tri n)) ∧ sumPow 5 1 = 1 ∧ sumPow 5 2 = 33 ∧ sumPow 5 4 = 1300 record
  6. the_chinese_remainder_theorem_holds_exactly_when_the_moduli_are_coprime — (List.range' 1 9).all (fun m => (List.range' 1 9).all (fun n => crtCoversAllPairs m n == (Families.gcd' m n == 1))) ∧ (List.range 105).filter (fun x => x % 3 == 2 && x % 5 == 3 && x % 7 == 2) = [23] record
  7. eight_and_nine_are_the_only_consecutive_perfect_powers_below_two_thousand — (List.range' 1 1999).filter (fun n => pp2000.contains n && pp2000.contains (n + 1)) = [8] ∧ pp2000.length = 55 ∧ pp2000.contains 8 = true ∧ pp2000.contains 9 = true record
  8. two_twenty_and_two_eighty_four_are_the_smallest_amicable_pair — aliquot 220 = 284 ∧ aliquot 284 = 220 ∧ (List.range' 2 218).all (fun a => ¬ (aliquot (aliquot a) == a && ¬ (aliquot a == a))) ∧ (List.range' 2 218).filter (fun a => aliquot a == a) = [6, 28] record
  9. the_two_power_sums_are_one_sum — ∀ p n : Nat, sumPow p n = powSum p n record
  10. nicomachus_sum_of_cubes_is_the_square_of_the_triangular_number_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, sumPow 3 n = tri n * tri n record
  11. the_sum_of_fifth_powers_has_the_closed_form_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, 12 * sumPow 5 n = n * n * (n + 1) * (n + 1) * (2 * n * n + 2 * n - 1) record
